spatial_claims.claim: O is the midpoint of AB, the center of the given sphere
C lies on AB with CB = AB/3 and AC = 2AB/3, so C is between A and B closer to B
D lies on semicircle ADB, obtained by erecting perpendicular from C to AB
Angle ADB is a right angle (D on semicircle with diameter AB)
DC is perpendicular to hypotenuse AB in right triangle ADB; similar triangles yield AD^2 = AC*AB and CD^2 = AC*CB
Circle with center C and radius CD lies in a plane perpendicular to AB at C; AB is perpendicular to this plane
F, G, H lie on circle centered at C with radius CD in the plane perpendicular to AB; CF = CG = CH = CD
Angle ACF is a right angle because AB is perpendicular to the plane containing CF
AF = AG = AH = AD, all computed via right angle at C between AC and radii CF, CG, CH
FG = GH = HF = AD, so all six edges of tetrahedron AFGH are equal
O lies between A and C on segment AB, with OC = CB/2
OF = OA (circumradius), verified via right angle at C between OC and CF
OG = OH = OA, so F, G, H all lie on the sphere centered at O

configuration_map: Configuration: AB is a diameter of the sphere with center O at midpoint. C divides AB such that AC:CB = 2:1. D is the foot of the perpendicular from the semicircle on AB down to C (i.e., D is where the perpendicular at C meets the semicircle). In 3D, a plane perpendicular to AB passes through C; a circle of radius CD is drawn in this plane centered at C. Equilateral triangle FGH is inscribed in this circle. The tetrahedron AFGH has apex A and base FGH. Key measurements: CB is the unit; AC = 2CB, AB = 3CB, AO = 3CB/2, OC = CB/2, CD^2 = 2CB^2, AD^2 = 6CB^2, FG^2 = 6CB^2. The circumcenter O lies on segment AC at distance 3CB/2 from A, which is 3/4 of the height AC = 2CB from apex A to base plane -- the correct circumcenter position for a regular tetrahedron.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The construction places the base equilateral triangle FGH in a plane perpendicular to diameter AB at point C, with vertex A at one endpoint of the diameter. Every distance computation (AF, AG, AH, FG, GH, HF) correctly uses the right angle at C between the diameter direction and radial directions in the base plane, yielding all six edges equal to AD. The sphere inscription is verified by showing OF = OG = OH = OA using the same right-angle configuration. The circumcenter O at 3/4 of the apex-to-base height is the correct position for a regular tetrahedron. No angle decomposition errors, no inside/outside contradictions, no betweenness violations.
